target_customer: Smartphone users who want personalized emoji and stickers, paying through app subscriptions
problem: Standard emoji do not look like the sender. Mirror turns a selfie into a large set of personalized emoji for messengers.

founders.name: Serge Faguet
founders.background_notes: Named as CEO and co-founder by Crunchbase News in December 2017. Not listed on the YC page. No background given in the article.

competitors.name: Bitmoji
competitors.what: Personalized cartoon avatar and emoji app owned by Snapchat
competitors.traction_then: Keyboard launched October 2015 and Snapchat integration

competitors.name: Apple Animoji
competitors.what: Face-tracked animated emoji launched with iPhone X
competitors.traction_then: Launched with the iPhone X in late 2017

technical_complexity.rationale: Generating many personalized emoji from one selfie needed face analysis and GPU inference. NVIDIA's blog says it ran on NVIDIA GPUs on AWS with Caffe, which was feasible for a small team in 2017.

defensibility.rationale: Selfie-to-avatar features were copyable. Google added selfie stickers in Gboard and Apple shipped Animoji and Memoji.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Google launched selfie-based Mini stickers in Gboard in 2018 and Apple added Memoji, absorbing the wedge.

market_need_then: Personalized emoji was a hot category in 2017, with Bitmoji's popularity and Apple's Animoji launch. Crunchbase News called 2017 the year of the AI emoji craze.

branding.domain_note: Uses mirror-ai.com rather than a bare mirror.com.

identity.mascot_or_character: Personalized emoji of the user's own face

branding.community_and_virality: Celebrity investors such as Kevin Durant drew coverage at launch. No merch or fan evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Name is simple and descriptive of the idea, but the brand drew little press beyond launch and celebrity backers.

outcome_analysis: Mirror AI raised a $3.5M seed in December 2017 at a claimed $30M valuation and launched a beta that month. Google's selfie stickers in Gboard and Apple's Memoji covered the same wedge, and no later round or growth numbers were found. The YC page lists it as active with seven people, and an app listing shows a 2024 copyright, so it persists as a small app. The cause of stalling is inferred, not stated by the company.
notes: Site mirror-ai.com could not be fetched because the host is outside the session network allowlist. Round is cross-checked only via aggregator sources (StartupIntros says $4M announced December 1, 2017, CB Insights says December 13), so the amount and valuation come from one article and the stage label seed from CB Insights. Faguet is not on the YC page but named by Crunchbase News. One profile names other founders (Kochukov, Kondratyeva) and was disregarded. The valuation is the company's own claim. No outcome news was found, and failure_factors are an inference from competitor timing.
